differences.cause: The native encoder refuses a longitude of 180 degrees, a track number above 4095 and an altitude outside -1500 to 150000 ft. The pack writes any value the field holds; longitude 180 is written as 2^25.

MRH. goat-transformers sets MRH to 1 when I062/130 is written (derive cat062.mrh present hae, its spec 0.12, goat-transformers#105); the native encoder writes 0. The 24 inputs are the encoded tracks with an altitude.
The native encoder omits a zero fraction of a second; the library always writes milliseconds. The instant is the same.

The native encoder's WGS84_E2 is the rounded 6.694_379_990_14e-3; goat-transformers spec 0.16 takes e2 = f(2 - f) = 0.0066943799901413165. The meridional radius depends on 1 - e2, so the degrees of latitude differ by about 1.6e-15 relative. x_error is equal on every input.
The native encoder writes one object_info per identifier whose scheme is sapient-object-info, with the constant type rcs_dbsm. The pack does not map the identifiers list to object_info.
The native encoder writes one object_info per identifier whose scheme is sapient-object-info. The pack does not map the identifiers list to object_info.

At a whole second the native encoder omits nanos; the library writes the 0 it derives from time_ms (sapient 0.2.0, sec_of and nsec_of). Timestamp.nanos is a proto3 field without presence, so 0 and absent are the same value.
